title: A staged plan is not a dispatch problem: an un-dispatched task is never observed
reported_by: the user, 2026-09-16, as the console burst pasted in the session

defect.observed: 12 console lines `NEVER-STARTED mpd-default task=t1 member=Planner attempt=(none) …` on host start, and again on the next host start (measured bursts at 03:41:08.696Z, 03:41:23.696Z, 03:41:38.700Z, 03:42:33.225Z)
defect.record_under_observation: .mpd/team/mpd-default/team.json — phase "staged", planReviewState "awaiting_review", no approvedAt, 12 tasks all pending with an assignee and ZERO attempt ids (43986 bytes)
defect.mechanism: candidateFor() filtered on assignee + non-terminal status only, so an un-dispatched task became a silence candidate; the machine classifies 'no stamp ever written for this task' as never-started, which the engine records ONE incident and ONE console line for
defect.class: false positive (the same class as r4's dead-team flood and r6's long-tool false positive), reached through the candidate set instead of the liveness gate

fix.rule: a task is observed only when it was HANDED TO SOMEBODY AT SOME POINT: a non-empty attemptId (written by lib/scheduler.js beginTaskAttempt at dispatch, before delivery) OR any stamp of its own, of any generation, scoped to this team (a stamped task WAS worked on, even when its attempt was later revoked/amended and the id cleared — the candidacy test therefore reads the UNFILTERED stamps, unlike the W11-2 slice that answers 'is the CURRENT generation silent')
fix.untouched: the WARN→ESCALATE machine, streak keys, holds, scenes, the r4 liveness gate, the tool-in-flight rule, the adopted plugin, skills/**

intermediate.note: an intermediate revision (e87da13c…, 125398 B) was measured and then revised after the independent review: its stamp half used the W11-2-FILTERED slice, which hid a task whose attempt had been revoked after it was worked on

tests.failing_first: RED on the pre-fix source: raw/red.log shows the staged case producing 12 incidents (expected 0) and candidateFor returning t1 for an un-dispatched task
cases: 12 pending assigned tasks, no attempt and no stamp: no record, no console line, no hold
CONTROL: the same record with dispatch attempts still reports every never-started task (12 records, no hold)
a REVOKED generation (attempt cleared, one old stamp) stays observable — and only that task does
candidateFor: an un-dispatched task is not a candidate; a dispatched one is
candidateFor: a stamp for the task keeps it observable even without a live attempt
candidateFor: an EARLIER generation's stamp still proves the task was worked on; another TEAM's does not

honest_limits: A task whose attempt was cleared AND that carries no stamp at all (a first delivery that failed before the member's first stamp, lib/scheduler.js:669-687) is indistinguishable on disk from a staged task and is now silent; a task that HAD been stamped stays observable (measured: the revoked row).

A task the scheduler never dispatched although its dependencies were met is also silent: TeamTask carries no `dependencies`, so 'ready but never dispatched' cannot be told from 'blocked on dependencies'. A future wave that wants that signal must read `dependencies` and require every dependency completed.

The never-started dedupe is still per process (neverStarted is in-memory), so a genuinely dispatched task whose owner never stamped is re-reported after a restart — intended, since it is a real observation.
The panel's read watermark is a single reader key; other readers keep their own replay by design.
